claims.text: A rollback undoes only a transaction that is still open; once a transaction commits, its changes cannot be rolled back.

claims.text: On a refusal, RecordResult sets the refund row's Status to failed and FailureReason to the gateway's reason and returns a payment.refund-failed outbox message; SendDueAsync saves both in one transaction. No row is deleted.

PaymentEventsConsumer.HandleAsync calls OrderService.FailRefundAsync on payment.refund-failed; the order's change, its inbox row and the order.refund-failed outbox row are saved by one SaveChangesAsync.
Order.FailRefund() accepts only a refunding order (code not-refunding otherwise), sets Status to paid and records OrderRefundFailed; CompleteRefund() has the same check and sets cancelled.

OrderRefundFailed leads to an order.refund-failed outbox row (NotifyCustomerOnOrderEvents) and a refund-failed | paid row in order_status_history (RecordOrderStatusHistory), which adds one event | status-after row per saga change (refund-requested | refunding).
Notifications turns order.refund-failed into an email with the subject 'refund failed'; a paid order can be shipped again (Ship() accepts paid).
GET /api/v1/refunds?status=failed is served by DonHang.Payments behind the StaffOnly policy: staff get 200 with order 3, its amount and failureReason; customer 2 gets 403.

When HandleAsync throws a non-poison exception, PaymentEventsConsumer waits RequeueAfter and nacks with requeue: true, so the message is tried again; a PoisonMessageException is rejected with requeue: false and goes to the dead-letter queue.

claims.text: Running refund-declined.sh prints 202; history refund-requested | refunding then refund-failed | paid; now: paid; refund | failed | 1 | <reason> (kind, status, attempts, failure_reason); emails 'refund requested' and 'refund failed' both sent; 200 for staff, 403 for customer 2.
The refund requirements ask that staff see each refund the gateway refuses in a list (YC-6).

Opinion: when a saga step cannot be rolled back, undo its business effect with a new, recorded change and keep the failed records; when a step's effect has left the system (money returned, email sent), push the later steps forward instead of trying to undo it.

RefundRequestedConsumer saves a pending refund row in its own transaction without calling the gateway; RefundSender calls the gateway later, so the order's refunding change and the pending refund row are committed before the gateway answers.
